info.title: Drop Cowboy Public API
info.description:
The Drop Cowboy® API sends ringless voicemail, texts, email, voice broadcasts and
AI calls, and manages the contacts, campaigns, phone numbers and AI agents behind
them. The base URL is `https://api-v2.dropcowboy.com`.

## Authentication

Send your API key and secret as the `x-key` and `x-secret` headers. You can use an
OAuth 2.0 client-credentials token from `https://login.dropcowboy.com/oauth/token`
instead, as `Authorization: Bearer`; each operation lists the scope it needs.

## Responses and errors

Successful responses are `{"data": ..., "meta": {"request_id": ...}}`, and errors
are RFC 9457 problem details with the same `request_id`. Branch on the HTTP status,
and retry `429` and `5xx` with exponential backoff and jitter.

## Asynchronous sends

`POST /rvm`, `/sms`, `/voice-broadcast` and `/ai-broadcast` answer `202` and check
your credentials and payload afterwards, so a `202` doesn't mean the send will
succeed. The result arrives on your `callback_url` and on the status webhooks.

## Guides

- [Send lifecycle](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/send-lifecycle)
- [Webhooks](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/webhooks)
- [Outcomes](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/outcomes)
- [Troubleshooting](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/troubleshooting)
- [Responses, errors and limits](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/errors-and-limits)

servers.description: Public REST API. Detection and Building Blocks widget operations set their own server.

get.description:
The OpenAPI 3.1 document for this API. No credentials. Responses carry
`ETag` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`. A matching `If-None-Match`
returns `304` with an empty body. The same file is published at
`https://www.dropcowboy.com/openapi.yaml`.

ETag.description: SHA-256 of the document, a quoted strong validator.

304.description: The document has not changed since the `If-None-Match` value.

get.description:
Page with `limit` and `offset`. The page is `data.contacts`, and
`data.total_contacts` counts every match.

parameters.name: list_id
parameters.description: Only contacts on this list.

parameters.name: search_term
parameters.description: Free-text search across field values, such as a name, phone number or email.

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description: Only contacts with this disposition id. `none` returns contacts without one.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Only contacts owned by this user id. `__unassigned__` returns contacts with no owner.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Only contacts of this brand. Without it you get every brand.

post.description:
Creates one or more contacts. Describe your columns once in `fields`, then send one
row per contact in `values`. A row that matches an existing contact by `record_id`,
email or phone number updates that contact instead, following `conflict_mode`. Every
row needs a `record_id`, an email or a phone number; rows without one are rejected.
By default no webhooks are sent and no automations start.

201.description: Per-row results, or totals when `return_counts` is true.

get.summary: Search contacts by phone or email
get.description:
Exact match on `phone`, `email`, or both. At least one is required; a request
with neither answers `400`. To search by name, use `search_term` on
`GET /contact/public/contacts`. Page with `limit` and `offset`.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Matched without regard to case.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Only contacts of this brand.

200.description: Matching contacts. No match returns an empty `contacts` array.

get.description:
Returns everything about one contact in `data.contact`: field values, phone numbers,
lists, tags, pinned notes, consent and do-not-contact flags. An unknown id still
answers `200`, with `data.contact` set to `null`.

put.description:
Changes field values. Send standard fields by name, such as `first_name`, `email` or
`main_phone`, at the top level of the body or inside `contact`; each one updates the
contact's field of that type, or adds it. For custom fields, or to target one field by
id, send `contact.field_data` entries with the `field_id` from
`GET /contact/public/contacts/{id}`. A `field_data` entry wins over a standard field
of the same type. Phone numbers are stored in E.164, and one that can't be read is
left out. A body with nothing to update is a `400` (`details.code`
`no_updatable_fields`). Lists, tags, the owner and the disposition have their own
routes. The response is the updated contact as stored.

fieldData.summary: Field values by field_id, including a custom field

delete.description:
Deletes the contact. It no longer appears when you list, search or get contacts.
The response is the deleted contact with `deleted_at` and `deleted_by` set.

post.description:
Adds the contact to each list in `list_ids`, one list at a time in the order given.
Repeated ids are added once. Each list sends its own `contact.list.added`. If adding
to a list fails, the request stops there and returns the error: lists earlier in
`list_ids` keep the contact and later ones are not attempted. On success
`data.contact` is the updated contact, as in `GET /contact/public/contacts/{id}`.

list_ids.description: The lists to add the contact to. A missing or empty array, or any id that is not a non-empty string, is a 400.

delete.summary: Remove a contact from a list
delete.description:
Removes one contact from one list. A contact whose brand differs from the list's
brand is skipped, and the response reports how many were skipped.

post.description:
Adds the contact to `to_list_id` and removes it from `from_list_id`. If the target
list belongs to a different brand than the contact, the contact stays where it is
and is counted in `skipped`.

post.summary: Add a tag to a contact
post.description:
Adds an existing tag to the contact. Adding a tag the contact already has is safe.
The response lists the contact's tags after the change. An unknown contact or tag
returns `404`.

delete.summary: Remove a tag from a contact
delete.description:
Removes the tag from the contact; the tag itself still exists. The response lists the
tags the contact still has, which can be empty. An unknown contact or tag, or a tag
the contact doesn't have, returns `404`.

get.description: Returns every tag on your account.

parameters.name: search_term
parameters.description: Filter tags whose label matches (case-insensitive substring).

post.description:
Creates a tag. Send a `label` and, optionally, a `color` and a `text_color` as hex
values. The response is the new tag, and its `tag_id` is the id you use to refer to it.

201.description: Tag created. The tag's id is `tag_id`.

put.description: Changes only the fields you send. Always send `label`, even when you change only the colors.

delete.description:
Deletes the tag, which then no longer appears in `GET /tag/public/tags`. Contacts
that had the tag are not updated, so their `tags` can still hold its id.

post.description: Deletes every tag in `tag_ids`. Ids that aren't on your account are skipped without an error.

get.description:
Returns every note on the contact, pinned or not, newest first. `username` is the
author's name.

username.description: The author's first and last name.

post.summary: Add a note to a contact
post.description:
Adds a note. `note` can contain basic HTML, which is sanitized. New notes aren't
pinned, and `GET /contact/public/contacts/{id}` returns only pinned notes.

get.description:
Returns all of the contact's follow-ups in one response, soonest first. Cancelled
follow-ups are left out unless you ask for them with `status`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only follow-ups with this status.

post.description:
Schedules a reminder to get back to the contact. When it's due, the follow-up becomes
`triggered` and creates an Inbox task for whoever it's assigned to.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `followup_id` of the follow-up.

put.description:
Changes when it's due, what it says, or who it's assigned to. Send only the fields you
are changing. Only pending follow-ups can change; any other status is a `409`. To
close one, cancel it with `DELETE /contact/public/follow-ups/{id}`.

delete.description: Cancels a pending follow-up so it never becomes a task. Any other status is a `409`.

put.description:
Makes a user the contact's owner. Only the current owner or a manager can change the
owner of a contact someone else owns. The response is the updated contact as stored.

owner_id.description: User id of the new owner.

put.description:
Records a disposition on one contact. Send the `disposition_id` of the disposition to
record. The response is the updated contact, whose `disposition` field holds the latest
one.

disposition_id.description: Id of the disposition to record. A missing, empty or non-string value is a 400.

200.description: Disposition set. The response is the updated contact as stored.

get.description:
Returns every consent record for the contact in one response, newest first, including
opt-outs and revocations. An unknown contact returns an empty array.

post.description:
Stores a consent record and updates the contact's consent flags. Send `phone_number`,
`email`, or both. Opt-out types (`tcpa_optout`, `sms_optout`, `email_optout`) record
a revocation and send no `contact.consent.granted`.

put.description:
Records a `tcpa_optout` for the phone number and email on the consent `cid`, revokes
the contact's TCPA consents, and adds every phone number on the contact to your
do-not-contact list. Revoking an `esign` consent revokes all of the contact's
consents. The response is the new opt-out record. A `cid` that doesn't exist leaves
no phone number or email to opt out, which is a `400`.

ip_address.description: The contact's IP address. Defaults to the caller's.

user_agent.description: The contact's browser user agent. Defaults to the caller's.

get.description:
Returns every custom field on your account in one response, newest first. Use
`custom_field_id` as `field_id` when you create contacts with a `custom_field` column.

Page with `limit` and `offset`. The page is `data.lists`. The built-in Unlisted list,
which holds contacts on no other list, is moved to the front of whichever page it
falls on. Each list carries `contact_count`; for line-type and other counts, get the
list with `GET /contact/public/lists/{id}`.

parameters.name: search_term
parameters.description: Only lists whose name matches.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Only lists of this brand.

post.description:
Creates an empty list. List names are unique on your account; a duplicate name is a
`409`. The response is the stored list, without counts.

get.description: The list, with its counts, is in `data.list`.

put.description:
Changes only the fields you send. The response is the updated list as stored,
without counts.

delete.description:
Deletes the list. Its contacts stay on your account unless you send
`delete_contacts: true`, which needs permission to delete contacts. System lists
can't be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `list_id` from `GET /contact/public/lists`.

get.description:
Cursor pagination, oldest first. Pass `next_cursor` back as `after_id` until
`has_more` is false. Operation webhooks such as `contact.list.added` carry a
ready-made `more_via` URL for this route.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Values above 500 are treated as 500.

next_cursor.description: Send as `after_id` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

get.summary: Check numbers or emails against the do-not-contact list
get.description:
Send `phone_numbers`, `emails` or both. `on_dnc` is true when any of them is
listed. With `brand_id`, entries for that brand and entries that apply to
every brand both count.

parameters.name: phone_numbers
parameters.description: Comma-separated phone numbers in E.164 format.

parameters.name: emails
parameters.description: Comma-separated email addresses. Matching ignores case.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Check as this brand.

post.summary: Add numbers or emails to the do-not-contact list
post.description:
Adds or updates one entry per number and email, and flags matching contacts
as do-not-contact. Without `brand_id` the entries apply to every brand.
Adding something already listed for the same brand updates its entry and
is reported in `already_listed`.

post.summary: Remove several numbers or emails from the do-not-contact list
post.description:
Removes each number and email and clears the do-not-contact flag on matching
contacts. Opt-outs the recipient made themselves (for example a STOP reply)
are kept and reported in `skipped`.

parameters.name: phoneNumber
parameters.description: The number exactly as it was added, in E.164 format.

get.summary: Check one number against the do-not-contact list
get.description:
Returns the matching entries when the number is listed, and `404` when it
isn't. To check several numbers or emails at once, use `GET /dnc/public/dnc`.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Check as this brand. Entries for that brand and entries that apply to every brand both count.

delete.summary: Remove a number from the do-not-contact list
delete.description:
Removes the entry and clears the do-not-contact flag on matching contacts,
and returns the entry that was removed. Returns 400 if the recipient opted
out themselves. A number that isn't listed still returns 200, with
`deleted_at` and `deleted_by` set to `null`.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Brand of the entry to remove. Without it, the newest matching entry is removed.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: The email address. Matching ignores case.

get.summary: Check one email against the do-not-contact list
get.description:
Returns the matching entries when the address is listed, and `404` when it
isn't.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Check as this brand. Entries for that brand and entries that apply to every brand both count.

delete.summary: Remove an email from the do-not-contact list
delete.description:
Removes the entry and clears the do-not-contact flag on contacts with that
email, and returns the entry that was removed. Returns 400 if the recipient
unsubscribed themselves. An email that isn't listed still returns 200, with
`deleted_at` and `deleted_by` set to `null`.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description: Brand of the entry to remove. Without it, the newest matching entry is removed.

get.description:
Returns every number on the account in one response, with the account's number
limits. Released numbers, dial-in numbers and 911 callback numbers are left out.
This route isn't paged.

200.description: Every number on the account in one response, with the account's number limits.

post.description:
Finds numbers you can rent with `POST /phone/public/numbers/rent`. A search buys
nothing and changes nothing. It needs the `numbers:read` scope.

What it searches depends on the account:

- **Building Blocks (BYOC) accounts** search the live inventory of the connected
  carrier, so every result is a number that carrier can sell you. Search works for
  Twilio, Commio (ThinQ) and Sinch. A Telnyx carrier answers with an empty list,
  and the other carriers don't support search: buy those numbers at your carrier
  and load them with `POST /phone/public/numbers/import`. An account with no
  connected carrier fails with `400` and code `byoc_not_configured`.
- **Other accounts** search Drop Cowboy's shared inventory. They can rent from it
  only during the trial period.

The answer is always a list in `data`. Every item has `phone_number` in E.164.
The other fields depend on where the result came from: see `AvailablePhoneNumber`.
Results carry no price. Check capabilities in `features` or `capabilities` on each
result, because `services` and any other field not listed below is ignored.

`pattern` is an area code (three digits in the US and Canada). On a BYOC account a
longer string of digits matches numbers that contain it. On other accounts a value
that isn't a valid area code for the country answers an empty list. Leave
`pattern` out to search the whole country.

200.description: The numbers found, at most `limit` of them. An empty list means nothing matched.

400.description:
A BYOC account has no connected carrier (`byoc_not_configured`), or the carrier
rejected the search.

post.description:
Rents the numbers in `numbers`. Accounts on Building Blocks rent from their own connected carrier (BYOC): connect a carrier first, or the call fails with `403`. A BYOC account with no default number pool fails with `400` and code `pool_required`. Other accounts can rent here only during their trial period; afterwards the call fails with `400` and code `use_cart_instead`. Going over the account's number limit fails with `403`.
On a BYOC account this buys each number from your connected carrier and puts it on a phone line. It does not load numbers you already own. Load those with `POST /phone/public/numbers/import`. To find numbers to rent, search with `POST /phone/public/numbers/available`. A single `number` is accepted in place of `numbers`.

Loads numbers you already own at your carrier onto one of your phone lines, so
calls can be sent from them. Building Blocks (BYOC) accounts only: any other
account fails with `403` and code `byoc_required`, and a BYOC account with no
connected carrier fails with `400` and code `pool_required`.

Nothing is bought and the carrier is not contacted. The numbers are taken as
you give them, so load only numbers you hold. A number already on another
account is not taken: it is counted in `conflicts` on the finished job, and the
rest still load.

The numbers attach to your default carrier pool and to the line in
`phone_line_id`, or your default voice line when you leave it out. A number
already on your account keeps its routing unless `overwrite_routing` is
`true`. The route answers `202` with a `long_job_id`. Poll
`GET /phone/public/numbers/import/{job_id}` until `status` is `completed` or
`failed`.

To receive calls on these numbers, point your carrier's trunk at us. Loading a
number does not change anything at your carrier.

400.description:
The request is invalid. The code says why: `invalid_phone_numbers` (a value is
not E.164; the refused values are named in the message), `pool_required` (no
carrier connected) or `phone_line_required` (no `phone_line_id` and no default
voice line). An empty list or more than 5,000 numbers has no code.

403.description:
The account is not on a BYOC plan (`byoc_required`), or the key lacks the
`numbers:write` scope.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The `long_job_id` returned when the import was accepted.

get.description:
Returns where a number import stands. `status` is `processing`, `completed` or
`failed`. `result` is set only when `completed`; `error` only when `failed`. A job
that belongs to another account, or is not a number import, returns `404`.
Accepts the number with or without the leading `+`. Returns 404 for a number not on the account.

put.description:
Changes the settings of one number on your account. Send only the fields you want
to change; a field you leave out keeps its value. A number that isn't on your
account answers `404` and nothing changes.

Moving the number to another phone line with `voice_ivr_id` is the same as
`POST /phone/public/lines/{line_id}/assign`, and the answer then carries the
`e911` change. A change fires the `number.updated` webhook.

The 911 callback number of a location can't be renamed or moved to a line or
campaign. That answers `400` with code `e911_elin_locked`.

rename.summary: Rename a number and turn texting on

callTracking.summary: Tag a number for call tracking

200.description:
Number updated. `data` is an empty object, or holds `e911` when the request
included `voice_ivr_id`.

get.description: An unknown `call_id` returns 200 with an empty object.

Returns a signed download link for the call's first recording, valid for five
days. Returns 404 when the call or its recording doesn't exist. Outside a trial,
the response holds only `recording_unavailable_reason` when your balance is below
zero now, or when it was too low to record at the time of the call.

Inbound texts and messages sent from the inbox or with
`POST /phone/public/sms/reply`. `POST /sms` sends are not stored here. An unknown
`sms_id`, or one that belongs to another account, answers `404`. Files are listed
under `mms_media`, with a download `url` once a file's scan is `clean`.

Stored messages recorded against the contact, inbound and outbound, newest first.
`POST /sms` sends are not included. A `contact_id` with no messages, or one that
is not on your account, returns an empty `smss`.

Reading the thread marks that contact's unseen messages as seen, with `seen_by`
set to `null`; no other contact's messages are touched. Messages in the response
still carry the `seen_at` they had before this read. A `skip` or `limit` that is
not a whole number in range answers `400` (`invalid-parameters`).

post.description:
Sends one text or MMS to one number and answers with the stored message. Unlike
`POST /sms` it is synchronous: media is fetched, stored and scanned (up to 12
seconds) before the answer, and media problems come back as HTTP errors. Media
limits are the same as on `POST /sms`; see
[MMS](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/texts#mms). Billed per file for MMS.

200.description: Sent. The body is the stored message.

400.description:
`type` `.../invalid-parameters`: bad `media_urls` or `media_ids`, more than 10
files, or a `media_id` that is not found. `type` `.../server-error` with status
`400`: missing `phone_number`, `caller_id`, or both `sms_body` and media; a
do-not-contact number; or no usable sender.

402.description: Account billing is past due. `type` is `.../server-error`.

413.description: `.../payload-too-large`: a file is over 1 MiB, or the files total over 5 MiB.

415.description: `.../unsupported-media-type`: a file is not JPEG, PNG, GIF, WAV or MP3.

422.description:
`.../media-fetch-failed`: a URL did not answer `200` in time, or redirected;
retry later. `.../media-blocked`: the malware scan flagged a file; do not retry.

500.description: `.../server-error`: storing a file failed. Retry later.

502.description: `.../server-error`: the malware scan could not finish. Retry later.

503.description: `.../media-scan-pending`: the scan did not finish in time. Retry after `Retry-After`; the retry reuses the finished scan.

get.description:
Phone lines group your numbers and decide how calls and texts to them are
handled. Use `ivr_id` as `phone_line_id` on sends and campaigns. Pass
`statistics=true` to get `sms_enabled_count` and `rcs_enabled_count`, which tell
you which lines can text.

post.description:
Creates a phone line on your account. Send a `name` and a `type`, and optionally
call-handling `rules`, `availability`, SMS settings, and the registered texting
`campaign_id` the line sends under. The response is the new line. Its `ivr_id` is the
`phone_line_id` used elsewhere.

get.description:
Returns one phone line by id, with its call-handling rules, availability and SMS
settings. Its `ivr_id` is the `phone_line_id` used elsewhere.

post.description:
Changes how the line answers (this route uses POST, not PUT). `rules` run during
business hours and `after_hour_rules` outside them, as set by `availability`.
Each array needs one step with `start_rule: true` (the call arrives) and one
with `end_rule: true` (no key pressed). Send the whole array you want; it
replaces the existing one.

To have an AI agent answer, use the `AI Agent` action with a published agent:
`{"start_rule": true, "action": "AI Agent", "action_data": {"agent_id": "..."}}`.
See [Receptionist](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/agents/ai-receptionist).

delete.description:
Deletes one phone line from your account. An id that isn't one of your lines answers
`404`.

post.summary: Assign a number to a phone line
post.description:
Points the number's calls and texts at this line. Returns 409 with code
`TN_ALREADY_ON_CAMPAIGN` when the number is registered to a different texting
campaign than the line's. A number not on your account returns `404` and
nothing changes.

confirm_move.description: Required to move a number onto a line that texts through an imported Twilio campaign when the number is on another campaign.

get.summary: List the numbers on a phone line
get.description:
Returns every number whose calls and texts follow this line. Released numbers
and the shared trial numbers are left out. The route isn't paged. A `line_id`
that isn't one of your lines gives an empty list, not `404`. To check the line
exists, call `GET /phone/public/lines/{line_id}`.

post.summary: Make a phone line the default
post.description:
Makes this line the account's default of its `type`. The line that was the
default of that type stops being it, so an account has one default per type. The
default line takes the numbers you add without a `voice_ivr_id`.

`type` must be the line's own type, as returned by `GET /phone/public/lines`. A
line that isn't yours, or whose type differs, answers `404` and the current default
stays. A system route, such as a 911 callback route, answers `400`.

200.description: The line is now the default. `data` is an empty object.

post.description:
Call from your server, never the browser. Returns a short-lived JWT (up to one
hour) that your page hands to a Building Blocks widget. `dialer:webrtc` and
`phone:hub` tokens need BYOC turned on and a positive balance. A site token
cannot mint another site token. `site_id`, when sent, must be a UUID, and it
is checked before the BYOC and balance gates.

Every refusal from those checks carries a stable snake_case reason in
`details.code`. Branch on it rather than on `type`, which stays the generic
status code (`bad-request`, `payment-required`, `forbidden`):

| Status | `details.code` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_site_id` | `site_id` was sent and is not a UUID. |
| 402 | `insufficient_balance` | No developer allotment left and no available balance. |
| 403 | `byoc_required` | `dialer:webrtc` or `phone:hub` was requested and BYOC is off. |
| 403 | `site_token_not_allowed` | The caller authenticated with a site token. |

A `403` without `details` is an authorization failure (the key lacks
`numbers:write`, or the signed-in user cannot edit phone numbers).

example.title: Bad Request
example.detail: site_id must be a UUID

402.description: No developer allotment and no available balance for a dialer or phone-hub token (`details.code` `insufficient_balance`).

example.title: Payment Required
example.detail: Insufficient balance for embed dialer usage.

403.description:
BYOC is off for dialer or phone-hub scopes (`byoc_required`), or the caller is
a site token (`site_token_not_allowed`). Without `details`, the key or user is
not allowed to mint.

value.title: Forbidden
value.detail: Building Blocks dialer requires BYOC. Enable BYOC on your team to mint embed tokens.

value.title: Forbidden
value.detail: A site token cannot mint another site token

get.description:
WebSocket upgrade. After it succeeds:

1. Send a text frame `{"type":"welcome","payload":{...}}` (see `DetectionWelcome`).
2. Wait for `{"type":"detection","event":"ready"}`.
3. Stream binary frames of mono audio (20 ms each) in the encoding and sample
   rate you declared.
4. Read text frames `{"type":"detection","event":"<name>","payload":{...}}`
   (see `DetectionEvent`). `detection` can be refined: act on the first result
   and treat later ones with `is_refinement: true` as corrections.
5. Send `{"command":"stop"}` when the call no longer needs detection. The
   server sends `close` for the session, then `stopped`, then closes the socket
   with code 1000 and reason `stop`. To pool sockets instead, set `keep_alive`
   in the welcome: the socket stays open after `stopped` for the next welcome,
   and is closed with 1001 `idle` if none arrives within 60 seconds. A socket
   that never sends a welcome is also closed after 60 seconds.

If you set `webhook` in the welcome, events are also POSTed to your URL, signed
with your Detection API key (see the `detectionEvent` webhook). Do not reconnect
mid-call: a new socket is a new session with no history.

parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: Alternative to the `Authorization` header when your client cannot set headers.

requestBody.description:
Not an HTTP body: the JSON text frames you send after the upgrade. Send the
welcome first; send stop to end the session.

101.description:
Switching protocols. The schema below describes the JSON text frames the
server sends on the open socket.

get.description:
Point a Twilio `<Stream>` here. Twilio cannot send headers, so pass the key and
options as `<Parameter>` elements:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `api_key` | Your Detection API key (required) |
| `webhook_url` | Where to POST events. When set, results go to the webhook instead of back on the stream |
| `webhook_events` | Comma-separated filter, for example `detection,beep,close` |
| `strategy` | `standard`, `beep_only` or `live_check` |
| `call_id` | Your own call identifier, echoed on every event |
| `detection_timeout_sec` | Give up after this many seconds (default 45) |

Audio is the stream's 8 kHz mu-law, so you don't need to transcode it.

The key is checked when the stream starts, not at the upgrade. If it is
missing, unknown, revoked or out of funds, the stream is closed with code
`1008` (`unauthorized`). Check the key's `status` with
`GET /register/public/detection-keys`.

post.description:
Two ways to add audio, both JSON:

- **From a URL.** Send `url`. We fetch the file and the entry is playable when
  this returns (`media_exists: true`).
- **Signed upload.** Send `signed_upload: true`. The response carries
  `upload.mp3` and `upload.wav`, each a signed `url` and the `content_type` to
  send with it. `PUT` the file bytes to one of them with that `Content-Type`,
  then call `POST /media/public/media/{media_id}/complete`. Until then the entry
  has `media_exists: false` and is hidden from the list.

Speech to text and voice cloning detect whether a `media_id` was uploaded as
MP3 or WAV, so you do not need to pass `ext` when you use it there.

(`media_exists: false`). A deleted entry returns `404`.

unknown or deleted `media_id` returns `404`.

deleted `media_id` returns `404`.

Call after the `PUT` to a signed upload URL succeeds. Marks the entry playable
(`media_exists: true`). Returns `400` when no file was uploaded yet.

send; until then `approved` is `false`.

Voice and messaging campaigns follow TCPA rules (calling hours, consent, your
account's contact frequency limit). Email campaigns follow CAN-SPAM
(unsubscribe link, physical address, email frequency limit). Accounts that have
not verified their brand get `403`; past-due accounts get `402`.

the `campaign_id` with List campaigns.

`risk` and `approved` are set by Drop Cowboy and ignored here. Changing what
contacts receive (message, audio, voice, AI agent, lists, brand, caller ID or
sending numbers) sends the campaign back to compliance review, and a sending
campaign that isn't approved again straight away is paused.

`campaign.completed`.

Campaign started, or held for compliance review. `started` is false when
nothing was queued. Starting a campaign that already completed returns it
unchanged with `started: true`. A campaign still waiting for review returns
`campaign_id`, `approved: false` and `started: false` and stays in the review
queue; start it again once it's approved.

billable counts, with the matching rates. Use `start_ts` and `end_ts` to limit the window
and `bucket_type` to choose how the results are grouped.

get.description:
Issues a new `proof_of_delivery_url` for one of your drops, for example after
the link you were sent has expired. Each call issues another link, valid for 7
days and never past the drop's 7-day window; earlier links keep working until
they expire. Proof of delivery is available for 7 days after the drop, so links
can be re-issued only within that time. `receipt_ready_at` is null while the recording
is not stored yet, and the link answers `404` with `Retry-After` until it is.

Only drops where a voicemail system took the call have one: a ringless voicemail
that ended with `reason_code` 0, 4001 or 4002, or a voice broadcast or AI call
that ended with 0 in a mailbox. Everything else, including another account's
drop or one more than 7 days old, answers `404`.

404.description: No proof of delivery for this drop.

example.title: Not Found
example.detail: No proof of delivery for this drop

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The last path segment of a `proof_of_delivery_url`.

get.description:
The `proof_of_delivery_url` itself. No credentials: the URL is the credential, so
treat it like a password and share it only with people who should hear the
recording. Opening it redirects to a short-lived audio URL (a few minutes), so
fetch the audio immediately rather than storing the redirect target. Each play
is recorded.

For a ringless voicemail, all three codes play the call recording, both sides,
from the moment the recipient's carrier answered until hangup. For code 0 it
includes your message. For 4001 (VoiceMail Not Setup) and 4002 (Mailbox full) it
contains the carrier's announcement, which shows the mailbox was reached and why
the message couldn't be left. For a voice broadcast or AI call it plays the
message left after the beep.

A link is valid for 7 days. After that it answers `410` for 7 days, then `404`.
Proof of delivery is available for 7 days after the drop, so store the audio
yourself if you need to keep it. Within those 7 days, get a new link with
`GET /campaign/public/deliveries/{drop_id}/receipt`.
Every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
Error bodies here are `{error, message}`, not problem details.

404.description:
Either the recording is not stored yet (`error` is `not_ready`, with
`Retry-After` in seconds; retry then), or the token is unknown or no longer
servable (`error` is `not_found`; do not retry).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Sent only with `not_ready`.

value.message: Proof of delivery is not available yet. Retry later.

410.description: The link has expired. Request a new one.

example.message: This proof of delivery link has expired. Request a new one from the API.

issues a new signing secret, so posting again is also how you rotate a secret or
move a URL. The `signing_secret` is returned here and by
`GET /register/public/account/webhook-signing-secret`.

`hook_type` and `hook_url` are not validated when you subscribe. Check the
event name against `GET /register/public/events` and use an HTTPS URL that
answers 2xx within 5 seconds. Only event types on that list are delivered
with signing and retries; any other `hook_type` is saved but gets no signed,
retried delivery. See [Webhooks](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/webhooks)
for signing, retries and deduplication.

event type as `hook_type`, not a `webhook_id`. An event type you have no subscription for
answers `404`.

post.description:
Turns on or off the setting that lets `POST /phone/embed/sms` and `POST /phone/embed/callback` send to a contact who already gave consent in Drop Cowboy. It is off by default, and while it is off every US send needs a `consent_id` from the consent widget.

When it is on and a request sends `contact_id` without `consent_id`, Drop Cowboy loads that contact from your account and uses its granted texting consent (for SMS) or calling consent (for callbacks). The destination must be one of the contact's own numbers, and the send is refused with `consent_required` if the contact has no granted consent for that channel, has opted out or replied STOP, or is on your Do Not Call list. A signed-in dashboard user also needs permission to edit the Trust Center.

get.description:
Each subscription has its own secret. Verify a delivery with the secret of the
subscription it arrived on, which is the event type in the payload's `event` field.

Secrets are never returned after creation. `last_used_at` and `request_count`
show which keys are still in use, which is what you check before deleting an old
key during rotation. `expires_at` is `null` for a key that never expires.

post.description:

before you do anything else. To rotate: create a new key, deploy it, confirm the
old key's `last_used_at` stops moving in `GET /register/public/apikeys`, then
delete the old key. For an agent or a one-off script, pass `scopes` and
`expires_in_seconds` to get a least-privilege key that removes itself. Trial
accounts get `403` with `trial_feature_blocked`. Only a verified account can
create keys: until verification is finished in the dashboard this returns
`403` with `team-not-verified`. Existing keys keep working.

expires_in_seconds.description: Lifetime of the key in seconds, from 300 (5 minutes) to 31536000 (365 days). The response's `expires_at` is when it ends. An expired key is refused by the API and deleted permanently, usually within two minutes of `expires_at`. Omit it, or send `null`, for a key that never expires. Anything else, including a string or a fraction, gets `400`.

returned after creation; `key_hint` is its last four characters so you can tell

store it before you do anything else. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`

balance, and a key stops working while the balance is empty. Requires Building

account can create keys (`403` with `team-not-verified`), and trial accounts get

To rotate: create a new key, deploy it, then delete the old one. A deleted key
can still open sessions for up to 60 seconds.

recordings short (a few minutes). Returns `402` when the account has no funds for
speech to text.

  uploaded MP3 answers `409`; retry after a few seconds. The upload's format is
  detected, so `ext` is optional. A `media_id` with no stored audio answers `404`.

16-bit), the audio is larger than 10 MB, or it could not be fetched or
transcribed.

post.description:
Sends one email from a mailbox on your verified sending domain. Give the
recipient as `to` or `contact_id`; a `to` address with no contact creates one.
Get `mailbox_id` from `GET /domain/public/mailboxes`.

The response is `200` whenever the request was well formed. Check
`data.success`: `false` with an `error` means nothing was sent (for example no
sending domain). Delivery, opens, clicks and bounces arrive on the
`contact.email.status` webhook.

Email has its own per-contact frequency limit, separate from the phone contact
frequency limit: by default 15 bulk emails per 3 days and 30 transactional
emails per 24 hours, configurable per account. Addresses on your email test
list are exempt.

With an `Idempotency-Key`, a successful send is stored for 24 hours and a retry
with the same key and body gets that stored response back with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`, without sending again. Only successes are stored:
a `200` with `success: false`, or an error status, releases the key, so a retry
with the same key sends again. An empty or whitespace-only header counts as no
header. A first request that stopped more than 15 minutes ago without finishing
releases the key: if it stopped before sending, the next retry sends; if it had
already sent the email, the retry gets `{"success": true}` with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The template send routes do not support
`Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
1 to 255 printable ASCII characters; a random UUID is the easy choice. Scoped
to your account for 24 hours from first use. Unlike the four send routes, an
empty value is rejected with `400`.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the stored response to an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`. Absent otherwise.

example.detail: Idempotency-Key must be 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters.

403.description: Scope missing, or the account's plan does not include email.

409.description:
`idempotency-key-reused`: the key was already used with a different body (or
on a different route); nothing was sent. `idempotency-request-in-progress`:
the first request with this key has not finished; retry shortly with the
same key. After 15 minutes an unfinished first request releases the key and
a retry goes through.

value.detail: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.

value.title: Idempotency Request In Progress
value.detail: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed. Retry later.

get.description: Shows whether your own carrier (BYOC) is connected. Carrier credentials are never returned.

post.description:
Connects your own carrier (BYOC) so you can send from your own numbers. Send the
carrier as `provider` and what it needs to sign in as `credentials`.

The call does the whole setup. It checks the credentials with the carrier, builds
the voice and ringless voicemail routes that point at your carrier's trunk, saves
the connection, and moves the account to a BYOC plan. After it returns, sends
route through your carrier. The route is part of the connection, not something
you pass on each send.

**The plan switch needs your say-so.** If the account is not on a BYOC plan yet,
the switch releases any phone numbers rented from Drop Cowboy and changes
billing. Send `confirm_leave_retail: true` to allow it, or the request fails with
`confirm-leave-retail-required` and nothing changes. Accounts already on BYOC
can leave it out. `plan_switched` in the response says whether the switch
happened on this call.

**Credentials by provider.**

| `provider` | `credentials` keys |
|---|---|
| `twilio` | `account_sid`, `auth_token` |
| `thinq` | `account_id`, `account_token`, `username`, `password` |
| `telnyx` | `api_key` |
| `signalwire` | `space_url`, `project_id`, `api_token` |
| `flowroute` | `access_key`, `secret_key` |
| `plivo` | `auth_id`, `auth_token` |
| `bandwidth` | `account_id`, `username`, `password`, `site_id`, `application_id` |
| `vonage` | `api_key`, `api_secret` |
| `sinch` | `project_id`, `key_id`, `key_secret` |
| `custom` | `carrier_name`, `sip_host`, `sip_port`, `username`, `password` |

Use `custom` for any SIP trunk not listed. `sip_host` is the trunk's hostname or
IP, `sip_port` defaults to 5060, and `username` and `password` are needed only
when the trunk uses credential authentication. A trunk that authenticates by
source IP leaves them out.

`channels` is the most calls your carrier lets you run at once and `cps` is how
many calls per second it allows. Set both to your carrier's real limits. Send
`enabled: true` and `default: true` to send on this carrier.

If the plan switch fails after the carrier was saved, the response is `502`
`plan-switch-failed`. Send the same request again to finish.

400.description:
The request is invalid. The code in `type` says why:
`unknown-provider` (`provider` is missing or not one of the listed carriers), `missing-credentials` (no `credentials`
object), `invalid-credentials` (the carrier rejected them), or
`confirm-leave-retail-required` (the account is not on a BYOC plan and the
request did not send `confirm_leave_retail: true`).

502.description:
`plan-switch-failed`: the carrier is connected, but moving the account to a
BYOC plan did not finish. Send the same request again to finish.

post.summary: Add a document to a knowledge base
post.description:
Three ways to add a document. The fields you send pick the method:

- `markdown` + `title`: inline text, up to 1 MB. Answers `201` with the document.
- `source_url`: Drop Cowboy fetches the file (up to 25 MB, public http(s) URLs
  only). Answers `201` with the document.
- `filename` + `mime_type` + `byte_size`: answers `201` with an upload ticket.
  PUT the file to `upload.url` with exactly the `Content-Type` in
  `upload.headers`, then call
  `POST .../documents/{knowledge_document_id}/uploaded`.

Every document is processed in the background. Poll the document list until
`ingest_status` is `ready` (or `failed`, with a reason in `ingest_error`).
Adding a file identical to one already in the knowledge base answers `409`, with
the existing document's id in `details.existing_knowledge_document_id`.

201.description: Document created, or an upload ticket when you sent `filename`

400.description:
Invalid request. With `source_url`, the `type` code says why the URL was
refused: `url-required`, `url-invalid`, `url-protocol-blocked` (not http or
https), `url-credentials` (user:password in the URL), `url-private-host`
(the host is or resolves to a private address), `url-unresolvable`, or
`empty-file` (the URL returned nothing).

example.title: Url Private Host
example.detail: The URL must point at a public host

409.description:
The same file is already in this knowledge base (`duplicate-knowledge-document`).
`details.existing_knowledge_document_id` names it.

413.description:
Content over the size limit: 1 MB for markdown, 25 MB for files
(`payload-too-large`), or the file at `source_url` is over 25 MB
(`url-too-large`).

415.description: `mime_type` not supported, the file extension does not match it, or `source_url` returned an unsupported type

502.description:
`source_url` could not be fetched (`url-fetch-failed`, including a non-2xx
answer from that server) or redirected too many times
(`url-too-many-redirects`). Nothing was added.

504.description: Fetching `source_url` timed out (`url-timeout`). Nothing was added.

post.description:
Call after the PUT to `upload.url` succeeds. Processing starts now. Answers
`409` if the upload was already confirmed (`already-confirmed`) or the file
duplicates one already in the knowledge base (`duplicate-knowledge-document`),
`413` if the stored file is over 25 MB, and `400` if no file was uploaded (PUT
it, then confirm again).

A duplicate `409` or a `413` marks the document `ingest_status: failed`, with
`ingest_error` set to `Uploaded file exceeds the 26214400 byte limit` or
`This document is already in this knowledge base`. PUT different bytes to
`upload.url` (or a new one from `POST .../upload-url`) and confirm again; a
successful confirm clears `ingest_error`. Or delete the document with
`DELETE .../documents/{knowledge_document_id}`. The other refusals
(`already-confirmed`, no file uploaded) leave the document unchanged.

413.description: The stored file is over 25 MB

post.summary: Get a new document upload URL
post.description:
Signs a new presigned PUT for a file upload that has not been confirmed yet:
its `upload.url` expired (after 48 hours), or a confirm was refused and you
want to send different bytes. The response has the same shape as the upload
ticket from `POST .../documents`. The URL writes the same file with the same
`Content-Type`, so PUT exactly the `upload.headers` and then confirm with
`POST .../uploaded`.

A document marked `ingest_status: failed` by a refused confirm goes back to
`pending`, with `ingest_error` cleared. A `pending` document is not changed.
Each call signs another URL, so retrying is safe; earlier URLs keep working
until they expire.

Once an upload is confirmed its file is fixed, so this answers `409`
(`already-confirmed`) whatever the document's `ingest_status`, and for
markdown and URL documents, which are confirmed when created. Delete the
document and add it again to replace it. Another account's document answers
`404`.

post.description:
Queues one ringless voicemail and answers `202` immediately. The credentials,
the payload and the recipient's consent are checked afterwards, so a `202` means
"queued", not "accepted". The outcome arrives on `callback_url` and on the
`contact.rvm.status` webhook. See [Outcomes](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/outcomes)
for every `reason_code`.

Each number counts toward your account's contact frequency limit (default
3 attempts in 3 days per number, across campaigns and dialer calls). Over the
limit the send fails with 4013 (Too Many Attempts), and the status webhook
carries `frequency_limit`. `max_attempts` and `max_attempt_window_ms` can make
the limit stricter for this send, never looser. Test numbers are exempt.

Results with `reason_code` 0 (Success), 4001 or 4002 carry a
`proof_of_delivery_url`, and `contact.rvm.receipt` fires once the recording
behind it can be played. It's available for 7 days. See
`GET /campaign/public/receipts/{token}`.

post.description:
Queues one SMS, one MMS when `media_urls` or `media_ids` is set, or one RCS

arrives on `callback_url` and on the `contact.sms.status` webhook. `message_id`
only confirms the request was accepted: the message isn't returned by
`GET /phone/public/sms/{sms_id}`, so track it through those results.

MMS: up to 10 files, 1 MiB each and 5 MiB in total, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WAV or MP3
(judged by the bytes). Each file is copied to `mms.dropcowboy.com`, scanned for
malware and sent only when clean; the copies are deleted after 3 days. Billed per
file; the caption adds no charge. You can send to any country your account
doesn't block. Media problems fail with 3032 to 3039. See
[MMS](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/texts#mms).

Outside the contact's allowed hours the message fails with 4011 (TCPA Hours) and
is not retried. Numbers over your account's contact frequency limit (default
3 attempts in 3 days) fail with 4013. A missing texting registration fails with
6009 (Unregistered Brand) or a pool error, and a `phone_line_id` whose line has no
texting campaign fails with 3029 (Phone Line Has No SMS Campaign); see
[Outcomes](https://www.dropcowboy.com/developers/api/outcomes).
