fails the send with 3019 (Invalid Callback). Otherwise the address is checked
just before the POST: if it is not http(s), does not resolve, or resolves to
a private, loopback or link-local address, the callback is skipped and the
send itself is unaffected. Redirects are not followed; a `3xx` is the final
answer.

postal_code.description: Recipient postal code. Improves the time-zone guess used for calling hours.

brand_id.description: Registered brand to send under. Required when your account enforces brand registration. See `GET /automation/public/brands`.

max_attempts.description:
Make the contact frequency limit stricter for this send: at most this many
attempts to the number within the window. Honored only when it is lower than
your account's limit (see `delivery_limits.frequency` on
`GET /register/public/account`); a higher or invalid value is ignored without
an error.

max_attempt_window_ms.description:
Make the frequency window longer for this send, in milliseconds. Honored only
when it is longer than your account's window; values over 30 days
(2592000000) are treated as 30 days. A shorter or invalid value is ignored
without an error.

phone_line_id.description:
Phone line the call is placed from; one of its numbers is shown as the
caller ID, picked per recipient. Return calls and texts reach that line and
follow its routing. Omit it to call from your default phone line; with no
default line the send fails with `4010`. When you send both, `caller_id` is
ignored. See `GET /phone/public/lines`.

caller_id.description:
BYOC accounts only. Your carrier's number in E.164, shown as the caller ID
exactly as given. Ignored on other accounts, which always call from a phone
line.

SendRvm.description:
Ringless voicemail. Give the audio as exactly one of: `media_id` (an uploaded or
recorded file), `tts_body` plus `voice_id` (text to speech), or `audio_url`
(BYOC accounts only; other accounts get "Not allowed audio_url").

**Sending on your own carrier.** Once a carrier is connected with
`POST /integration/public/byoc/connect`, the send needs no routing field: it goes
out on the connected carrier's trunk. Set `caller_id` to a number you own at that
carrier. It does not have to exist anywhere in Drop Cowboy, and it is shown
exactly as given. Host the audio at `audio_url` (a public mp3 or wav, up to
50 MB) and add `byoc` when you sign calls with STIR/SHAKEN.

Outside the contact's calling hours the voicemail is held and retried for up to
3 days, then fails with reason `tcpa_expired`.

tts_body.description: Text to speak with `voice_id`. Supports merge fields. Up to 1,200 characters once merge fields are filled in; longer text fails with `3021`.

audio_url.description: BYOC only. Public mp3 or wav URL, up to 50 MB, fetched when the voicemail is sent. Other accounts fail with 3014.

mobile_only.description: Skip numbers that are not mobile.

byoc.description: BYOC call options. Only for accounts on their own carrier.

sti_orig_id.description: The origination ID your carrier assigned for STIR/SHAKEN signing. Anything that is not a UUID fails with 3017.

sti_attestation.description: STIR/SHAKEN attestation level for the call. Anything else fails with 3018.

SendSmsMessage.description:
SMS, or RCS when `template_id` is given. Send from a `phone_line_id` whose line
has an approved texting campaign: that line picks the sender number and the
registered campaign. Without a phone line, a sender is picked from your
account's own texting numbers.

Give the content as `body` (plain text) or `template_id` (an RCS template built
in the dashboard; the template's fallback text is sent where RCS is unavailable).
If both are given, the template wins.

Add `media_urls` or `media_ids` (10 files in total) to send MMS. `body` is then
the caption and is optional. The caption is sent as written, with no opt-out text
added, and an MMS with no caption is sent as media only. A text-only `body`
without opt-out language gets ` Reply STOP to opt-out` appended. Media cannot be
combined with `template_id` (3032).
A send with no `body`, no `template_id` and no media fails with 3020.

Messaging is not held for calling hours: outside the contact's allowed hours the
send fails with reason code 4011 (TCPA Hours) and is not retried.

body.description: Message text, or the caption when media is attached.

template_id.description: RCS template. Turns this send into RCS. See `GET /template/public/templates?type=rcs`.

phone_line_id.description:
Phone line to send from. Its assigned numbers are used as the sender and
its approved texting campaign is used for routing. See
`GET /phone/public/lines`.

SendVoiceBroadcast.description:
Press-1 call. Plays one message to a live person and another to an answering
machine, and can transfer, confirm or opt out on a key press. Give content as
media (`media_on_*`) or text to speech (`tts_on_*` plus `voice_id`); `voice_id`
is required whenever any `tts_on_*` field is set. Calls from `phone_line_id`,
or your default phone line when it's omitted.

Outside the contact's calling hours the call is held and retried for up to
3 days, then fails with reason `tcpa_expired`.

media_on_speech.description: Media played when a live person answers.

media_on_beep.description: Media played to an answering machine.

media_on_confirm.description: Media played after the confirm key.

media_on_opt_out.description: Media played after the opt-out key.

tts_on_speech.description: Text spoken when a live person answers.

tts_on_beep.description: Text spoken to an answering machine.

tts_on_confirm.description: Text spoken after the confirm key.

tts_on_opt_out.description: Text spoken after the opt-out key.

transfer_digit.description: Key that transfers the call. Needs `transfer_ivr_id` or `transfer_to`.

transfer_ivr_id.description: Phone line that receives transfers. Preferred over `transfer_to`.

transfer_to.description: Number that receives transfers when no `transfer_ivr_id` is given.

opt_out_digit.description: Key that adds the number to your do-not-contact list.

max_ring_seconds.description: How long to wait for an answer before giving up.

amd_enabled.description: Detect answering machines and play the `*_on_beep` content after the greeting.

SendAiBroadcast.description:
Outbound call handled by one of your published AI agents. Build and publish the
agent first (`POST /agents/public/agents`, then `.../publish`). The send fails
with "No Agent", "Agent Not Active" or "Agent Is Draft" if the agent cannot take
calls. Outcomes arrive on `contact.rvm.status` with `campaign_type: ai_broadcast`
and, per call, on one `ai_agent.*` event (see the `/ai-broadcast` operation).

Outside the contact's calling hours the call is held and retried for up to
3 days, then fails with reason `tcpa_expired`.

voice_ids.description: Override the agent's voice for this call.

SendOutcome.description:
Body POSTed once to a send's `callback_url` when its outcome is known. Unsigned.
If the request fails validation before it is sent, a shorter body with
`status: failure`, `reason`, `reason_code`, `product_code`, `phone_number` and
`foreign_id` is posted instead.

proof_of_delivery_url.description:
Present when a voicemail system took the call: a ringless voicemail with
`reason_code` 0, 4001 or 4002, or a voice broadcast or AI call that ended
with 0 in a mailbox. See `GET /campaign/public/receipts/{token}`.
The `callback_url` body never carries `frequency_limit`; that is on the
status webhook only.

source.description: The system the event came from, for example `stripe`, `hubspot` or `custom-crm`.

contact_id.description: Direct contact ID (takes precedence over contact_lookup)

contact_lookup.description: Look up contact by email (tried first) or phone

external_url.description: Link to the event in the source system

client_event_id.description: Client-provided idempotency key (unique within 24h per team)

TimelineEntry.description:
One activity on a contact. Which other fields are present depends on `type`: notes
carry `note_id` and `note`, calls carry `call_id`, `direction` and `duration`, tag
changes carry `tag_id` and `tag_label`, consent changes carry the `consent_*` fields,
follow-ups carry `followup_id` and `data`, and integration events carry `source`,
`title` and `data`.

source.description: For integration events, the app that sent it.

user_id.description: The teammate who made the change.

campaign_type.description: The campaign's channel. Null when the campaign was saved without one.

list_ids.description: The contact lists the campaign sends to. Empty when it targets none.

delivery_type.description:
The campaign's delivery pacing with `-complete` appended, for example
`immediate-complete` or `drip-complete`.

campaign_type.description: The campaign's channel. Null when the campaign was saved without one.

list_ids.description: The contact lists the campaign sent to. Empty when it targeted none.

user_id.description: The teammate who made the change.

reason.description: Why the number was flagged. Always `complaint` today.

TeammateEventData.description: `data` for `user.created`, `user.updated`, `user.deleted`, `user.login` and `user.logout`. No credentials or tokens are ever included.

user_id.description: The teammate the event is about. For `user.updated`, the teammate who was edited.

updated_by.description: `user.updated` only. User id of the teammate who made the change; no record is attached for it.

paused.description: `true` when the subscription was paused, `false` when it was resumed.

SubscriptionInvoicedEventData.description: `data` for `subscription.invoiced`. No amounts or payment details are included.

invoice_id.description: The invoice number shown on the invoice in your billing history.

recurring.description: `true` for a regular renewal invoice, `false` for a one-off charge.

subscription_changed.description:
`true` when this renewal invoice was processed while a plan change on your
account was being applied, otherwise `false`. Always `false` for one-off charges.

status.description: The status the invoice just reached.

record_count.description: Number of result rows in the archive.

ftp_synced.description: `true` when your account copies archives to your FTP server.

step.description: The setup step being checked. `1` is the CNAME records, `2` the MX record.

error.description: A short description of what went wrong. Treat it as informational text, not a stable code.

user_id.description:
The teammate who opened or closed the task. Null when no teammate did, for example a
task opened by an inbound message.

contact_id.description:
The contact the task is about. Null, or absent along with `contact`, for a task with no
contact, such as an appointment booked without one.

user_id.description: The teammate who made the assignment.

contact_id.description: The contact the task is about. Null for a task with no contact.

assigned_to.description: The user id of the teammate the task is now assigned to. Not expanded into a record.

CallEventData.description:
`data` for `contact.call.ringing`, `contact.call.answered` and `contact.call.missed`.
Dialer calls (outbound) never carry `ivr_id`; inbound phone-line calls always do.

user_id.description: The dialer agent on outbound calls; on inbound calls the user the call is assigned to, absent when there is none.

contact_id.description: Null on an inbound call from a number that matches no contact.

list_id.description: The dialer list on outbound calls; usually null on inbound calls.

ivr_id.description: Inbound calls only. The phone line that was dialed.

CallHangupData.description: `data` for `contact.call.hangup`. Dialer calls never carry `ivr_id`; inbound phone-line calls always do.

ivr_id.description: Inbound calls only. The phone line that was dialed.

hangup_cause.description:
Telephony hangup cause, such as `NORMAL_CLEARING`, `USER_BUSY`, `NO_ANSWER`,
`ORIGINATOR_CANCEL`, or `NORMAL_TEMPORARY_FAILURE` when a dialer call could not be
placed. Always set on dialer calls; can be absent on inbound calls.

user_id.description: The dialer session's agent.

reason.description: Why the call was dropped. `no_agent` means no agent was free to take it.

user_id.description: The user the call is assigned to, absent when there is none.

contact_id.description: Null when the caller's number matches no contact.

ivr_id.description: The phone line that was dialed.

to.description: The phone line number that was dialed.

user_id.description: The dialer agent on `contact.call.disposition`; the teammate who made the edit on `contact.call.disposition.changed`.

contact_id.description: The contact the call was with.

list_id.description: The list the call was dialed from.

ivr_id.description: The phone line the call came in on. Null for dialer calls.

disposition_id.description:
Always sent. The disposition, a short token rather than a uuid: `sold`, `follow_up`,
`try_later`, `no_contact`, `no_interest`, `bad_lead`, `dnc`, `not_reachable`,
`network_blocked`, `no_service`, `no_answer`, `rejected`, `busy`, `skip`,
`redial`, `abandoned`, `voicemail`, `warm_transfer`, `cold_transfer`, `qa_fail`,
`qa_success`, `none`, or one of the team's custom slots `custom_1` to `custom_9`.

call_duration.description: Seconds. Can be fractional on the hangup-time `contact.call.disposition`; 0 when unknown. On `contact.call.disposition.changed`, the call's recorded duration.

call_direction.description: Always `outbound` on `contact.call.disposition`. On `contact.call.disposition.changed`, the call's own direction.

extension.description: The audio file's extension, with the dot, such as `.mp3`.

preview.description: Transcript of the contact's side of the recording. Can be long; not truncated to a short preview.

recording_session.description: Which recording session of the call this is, when a call was recorded in several sessions.

recording_transcript_part.description: Which part of a long transcript this is, when the transcript was split.

CallReadData.description: `data` for `contact.call.read` and `contact.call.unread`. `contact_id` is the contact on the call.

user_id.description: The teammate who changed the call.

AiAgentCallStartedData.description:
`data` for `ai_agent.call.started`. Inbound calls carry `direction: inbound`,
`call_id`, `from`, `to` and `ivr_id`. Outbound AI voice broadcast calls carry no
`direction`, and instead `campaign_id`, `session_id`, `drop_id` and `phone_number`.

agent_id.description: The AI agent handling the call.

from.description: Inbound calls only. The caller's number.

to.description: Inbound calls only. The phone line number that was dialed.

ivr_id.description: Inbound calls only. The phone line that was dialed.

drop_id.description: Outbound only. The send (a 24-character hex id), the same `drop_id` as on `contact.rvm.status`.

phone_number.description: Outbound only. The number being called, E.164.

ContactOperationData.description:
Fields on an event that covers many contacts at once. Only ids are sent, never
contact records: read a contact with `GET /contact/public/contacts/{id}`, or page
through a list with `more_via`.

total_count.description: How many contacts the change covered. Can exceed the ids sent.

truncated.description: True when `total_count` is more than the ids sent.

next_cursor.description: Cursor after the last id sent: pass it as `after_id` to `GET /contact/public/lists/{id}/contacts`. Null when not truncated. Absent on list copies and moves.

more_via.description: Link to the rest of the contacts: `GET /contact/public/lists/{id}/contacts` on `https://api-v2.dropcowboy.com`, with `after_id` and `limit=25` already filled in. Set only when the event is truncated and belongs to a list, including `contact.list.added` from an import into a list. Null otherwise: when not truncated, when the event has no list (such as `contact.created` and `contact.updated` from an import), and on list copies.

operation.description: The change behind the event. Absent on per-contact events, on web form events, and on events from `POST /contact/public/contacts`.

id.description: The import id for imports; otherwise matches the envelope's `operation_id`.

user_id.description: The teammate or API key owner who created the contacts. Absent when a web form, inbound call, text, email or chat created the contact, and on per-contact import events.

contact_ids.description: A single id (string) when one contact was created on its own; an array for contacts created together. An import sends at most 25; a `POST /contact/public/contacts` request sends every new id.

contact_id.description: Only on per-contact import events, in place of `contact_ids`.

source.description: How the contact was created: `manual` (app), `api` (`POST /contact/public/contacts`), `import` (a CSV import or another bulk create), `webform`, `call`, `sms` or `email`. Absent for contacts created by website chat and by some web form submissions.

user_id.description: The teammate who made the change. Absent for web form and per-contact import events.

contact_id.description: Set when one contact was edited.

contact_ids.description: Set instead of `contact_id` when creating contacts matched existing ones: a single id (string), or an array. An import sends at most 25.

user_id.description: The teammate who made the change.

owner.description: User id of the new owner. Null when the owner was cleared.

previous_owner.description: User id of the previous owner. Null when the contact had none.

disposition_id.description: The disposition now on the contact.

list_id.description: Present when the disposition was set from within a list.

reason.description: The reason given with the request; `user_request` when none was given.

deleted_by.description: User id of the teammate who made the request. No `user` record is attached.

contact_id.description: Absent when the consent was recorded for a phone number or email with no contact yet.

consent_method.description: How consent was captured, as given by the caller; `webform` for web form submissions.

phone_number.description: Not sent for web form consent.

email.description: Not sent for web form consent.

granted_at.description: Epoch milliseconds. Not sent for web form consent, which sends `created_at`.

consent_text.description: Web form consent only. The consent language the visitor agreed to.

page_url.description: Web form consent only. The page the form was on.

created_at.description: Web form consent only. Epoch milliseconds.

original_consent_id.description: The consent that was revoked, when the revoke named one. Not sent for email unsubscribes.

original_consent_type.description: Type of the revoked consent; `email_optin` for email unsubscribes.

consent_type.description: Web form opt-outs only. The opt-out type recorded.

phone_number.description: Not sent for email unsubscribes or web form opt-outs.

revoked_at.description: Epoch milliseconds. Web form opt-outs send `created_at` instead.

revoke_reason.description: How it was revoked, for example `api`, `manual`, `unsubscribe`, or `revoke_all` and `cross_channel_sync` when your compliance settings carried a revoke over from another channel.

created_at.description: Web form opt-outs only. Epoch milliseconds.

user_id.description: Absent for inbound faxes.
The teammate who acted, not necessarily the one the reminder is assigned to.

followup_id.description: The reminder. No reminder record is attached.

tag_id.description: No tag record is attached here; the contact's current tags are in `contact.tags`.

user_id.description: The teammate who requested the export.
The teammate or API key owner who made the change. Null for web forms; absent for list copies and moves and per-contact events.

previous_list_id.description: `contact.list.added` from a move in the app or API only: the list the contacts left.

contact_ids.description: Up to 25 ids, sorted by when the contacts were created. Empty for list copies and moves. A web form submission sends its one id as a string.

contact_id.description: Only on per-contact events, in place of `contact_ids`.

operation_id.description: Web form submissions only, which send it here rather than on the envelope.

action.description: Always `update`, including when the entry was just created.

board_id.description: The pipeline board. No board record is attached.

contact_ids.description: Up to 25 ids, sorted by when the contacts were created.

entered_at.description: When the contact entered the stage, epoch milliseconds.
When the contact entered the stage, epoch milliseconds.

board_id.description: The pipeline board when the list is a stage; null for a plain list.

entered_at.description: When the contact entered the list, epoch milliseconds.

AppointmentEventData.description:
`data` of every `appointment.*` event. `team` and `contact` are the records for
`team_id` and `contact_id`. Events with extra fields extend this schema.

booking_id.description: The appointment. For a group class, the class occurrence.

booking_type_id.description: The booking type (meeting or class template) it was booked on.

contact_id.description:
The contact the event is about. For a whole-class `appointment.cancelled` it
is null; see each event for who it names.

host_user_ids.description: The team members hosting it. Only ids; no user records are attached.

source.description:
Where the booking was made: usually `dashboard`, `public_page`, `embed`,
`ai_voice`, `ai_chat`, `automation` or `api`. Null on bookings that did not
record one.

join_url.description:
Video meeting link, when the booking has one. Always null on
`appointment.cancelled`, `appointment.waitlist.joined` and
`appointment.attendee.cancelled`. It is the live meeting link, so treat it as
you would a calendar invite.

location_type.description: How the appointment takes place. Null when the booking type has no location.

previous_start_at.description: The start time before the move, epoch milliseconds.

cancel_reason.description: The reason given when cancelling, if any. Free text.

attendee_count.description: Group class occurrences only. How many attendees the occurrence had.

changed.description: Names of the fields that changed. Today always `[join_url]`.

party_id.description: The party, meaning everyone booked together in one submission.

waitlist_position.description: The party's place in line, starting at 1. Null if it could not be determined.

party_id.description: The party that was moved off the waitlist.

attendee_id.description: The attendee's seat in the occurrence.

party_id.description: The party the attendee was booked with.

attendee_id.description: The attendee's seat in the occurrence.

party_id.description: The party the attendee was booked with.

cancel_reason.description: The reason given when cancelling, if any. Free text.

ReviewRequestEventData.description:
`data` of every `review_request.*` event. `team` is the record for `team_id`.
The contact is sent as a small nested `contact` object, not the full contact
record. Events with extra fields extend this schema.

contact.description:
The contact the request was sent to. `review_request.sent` also carries
`first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and `phone_number`, each null when
unknown; the other events carry only `contact_id`.

channel.description:
How the request was sent: `sms` or `email`. The value is passed through from
whoever created the request without validation, and anything other than
`email` is sent as a text.

source.description:
What created the request: usually `manual` (a team member), `automation`,
or `api`. Callers can set their own value.

source_event.description: The event that triggered an automated request, such as `appointment.completed`.

review_url.description:
The review page link sent to the contact. It contains a signed token that
lets anyone holding the link rate, leave feedback and click out as this
contact until it expires 30 days after sending. Do not publish it or pass it
to systems that should not act for the contact.

review_platform.description: The review site the contact was sent to.

feedback_text.description: The contact's feedback, trimmed and cut to 4000 characters.

FormSubmittedData.description:
`data` of `form.submitted`. `team`, `contact` and `list` are the records for
`team_id`, `contact_id` and `list_id`.

contact_id.description: The contact the submission was saved to, new or existing.

list_id.description: The list the form adds contacts to. Null when it has none.

page_url.description: The page the form was submitted from, when known.

form_fields.description: Each answered field, in form order. Fields left blank are omitted.

name.description: The field's name, such as `first_name` or a custom field slug.

label.description: The label shown on the form.

type.description: The field type, such as `text`, `email` or `phone`.

value.description: The answer. Phone numbers are E.164.

fields.description: The same answers as `form_fields`, keyed by field name.

ContactGoalAchievedData.description:
`data` of `contact.goal.achieved`. `team` and `contact` are the records for
`team_id` and `contact_id`. Goal settings the goal does not have are omitted.

goal_value.description: Sometimes present. The value you gave the goal; negative for goals that count against the score.

tag_ids.description: Tags the goal adds to the contact.

remove_tag_ids.description: Tags the goal removes from the contact.

list_ids.description: Lists the goal adds the contact to.

remove_from_list_ids.description: Lists the goal removes the contact from. `*` means every list.

visitor_id.description: The tracking script's id for the visitor's browser.

session_id.description: The browsing session, when the script sent one.

event_name.description: The tracked event that met the goal, such as `page_view` or `conversion`.

page_url.description: The page the event happened on, when known.

ProductInterestCapturedData.description:
`data` of `contact.product_interest.captured`. `team` and `contact` are the
records for `team_id` and `contact_id`.

visitor_id.description: The tracking script's id for the visitor's browser, when known.

product_id.description: Your product identifier, exactly as your site sent it to the tracking script.

price_cents.description: The price in the currency's minor unit (cents for USD), when your site sent one.

currency.description: Currency code as your site sent it, such as `USD`.

page_url.description: The page the interest was shown on, when known.

captured_at.description: When the interest was recorded, epoch milliseconds.

WebEventLinkedData.description:
`data` of `contact.web_event.linked`. `team` and `contact` are the records for
`team_id` and `contact_id`.

visitor_id.description: The tracking script's id for the visitor's browser.

linked_count.description: How many earlier website events were linked to the contact.

WebEventTrackedData.description:
`data` of `contact.web_event.tracked`. `team` is the record for `team_id`. No
contact is included.

visitor_id.description: The tracking script's id for the visitor's browser.

session_id.description: The browsing session. Omitted when the script did not send one.

site_id.description: The site the tracking script is installed on.

event_count.description: How many events from the batch were stored.

RvmSentData.description:
`data` for `contact.rvm.sent`. A voicemail sent from the app carries `rvm_id`; one
sent through the Drop Cowboy integration carries `integration_id` and `entry_id`
instead.

user_id.description: The teammate who sent the voicemail.

rvm_id.description: Voicemails sent from the app only.

entry_id.description: Drop Cowboy integration sends only. The contact timeline entry for the voicemail.

contact_id.description: Null when the number matches no contact.

phone_number.description: The number that opted out, E.164.

consent_id.description: The consent record that stores the opt-out.

number_id.description: Your number that received the text.

ivr_id.description: The phone line that received the text.

user_id.description: The teammate who set the disposition.

sms_id.description: The text the disposition was set on.

disposition.description: The new disposition: a built-in value such as `follow_up`, `sold`, `no_interest`, `bad_lead` or `dnc`, or the id of one of your custom dispositions.

user_id.description: The teammate who sent the email; null for campaign and automation sends without one.

entry_id.description: The contact timeline entry for the email.

user_id.description: The teammate the mailbox belongs to.

contact_id.description: The sender's contact.

mailbox_id.description: The mailbox the email arrived in; null for a shared inbound address.

contact_id.description: The contact who sent the email.

task_id.description: The inbox conversation the email belongs to.

email_id.description: The received email the link was in.

verdict.description: The threat check's result. `suspicious` links show a warning page first.

threat_types.description: What the threat check found; empty for a `safe` link.

user_proceeded.description: True when the teammate continued past the warning page for a `suspicious` link.

user_id.description: The teammate who sent or deleted the fax. Absent on `contact.fax.received`.

contact_id.description: Always null on `contact.fax.deleted`.

user_id.description: The teammate the call was assigned to, if any.

contact_id.description: Null when the caller matches no contact.

ivr_id.description: The phone line that was dialed.

user_id.description: The teammate who changed the voicemail.

chat_site_id.description: The chat widget the conversation came from.

email.description: The email address the visitor gave.

is_new.description: True when a new contact was created for the visitor.

chat_site_id.description: The chat widget the conversation came from.

RevenueContactData.description: Short summary of the contact the billing activity belongs to. This is not the full contact record, and the event does not attach one.

email.description: Omitted when the contact has no email.

main_phone.description: E.164. Omitted when the contact has no main phone.

RevenueEventData.description: `data` of the `revenue.*` events and `customer.trial.converted`. Money fields are integers in the minor unit (cents for USD) of the Chargebee currency; no currency code is sent. `team_id` is kept and its record attached as `team`.

event_type.description: Matches the webhook event. `customer.trial.converted` carries `subscription_started`, and `revenue.refund.created` carries `refund`.

amount.description: Minor units. The plan price or invoice total; negative for a refund and 0 for a cancellation.

mrr_impact.description: Change in monthly recurring revenue, minor units. Positive when a subscription starts or upgrades, negative on downgrade or cancellation, 0 on renewal and refund.

arr_impact.description: Change in annual recurring revenue, minor units. `mrr_impact` times 12.

previous_plan_id.description: Upgrades and downgrades only. The plan the contact moved off.

is_new_customer.description: True on the contact's first revenue event.

billing_provider.description: `chargebee` for every event from your Chargebee site.

chargebee_invoice_id.description: The invoice charged, or for a refund the invoice refunded. Null when no invoice was involved.

customer_tenure_days.description: Cancellations only. Days the contact was a customer.

churn_reason.description: Cancellations only. Chargebee's cancel reason, when it gives one.

is_trial_conversion.description: True when this subscription start converted a trial. This and the other trial fields are present only on events sent straight from Chargebee, not on held activity delivered after you link a customer.

subscription_status.description: Chargebee's subscription status when the event happened. Present only on events sent straight from Chargebee.

trial_start.description: Epoch milliseconds. Null when the subscription had no trial. Present only on events sent straight from Chargebee.

trial_end.description: Epoch milliseconds. Null when the subscription had no trial. Present only on events sent straight from Chargebee.

created_at.description: When the billing activity happened. Epoch milliseconds.

CustomerTrialExpiringData.description: `data` of `customer.trial.expiring`. `team_id` is kept and its record attached as `team`. Money fields are integers in the minor unit (cents for USD) of the Chargebee currency; no currency code is sent.

revenue_event.description: The contact's current trial. No revenue event is recorded for this webhook.

trial_potential_mrr.description: Monthly recurring revenue if the trial converts at its current plan, minor units.

CommissionEventData.description: `data` of the `commission.*` events. Money fields are integer cents. Only `team_id` is expanded (into `team`); `contact` and `recipient_user` carry ids only. On `commission.pending`, `goal` also carries the goal's `name`, `category` and `funnel_stage`, and `commission` carries only the fields set when it was created (no approval, rejection, payment or clawback fields, and no `modified_at`). Each event adds its own fields: `approved_by` (`commission.approved`), `rejected_by` and `reason` (`commission.rejected`), `paid_by` and `paid_at` (`commission.paid`).

user_id.description: The teammate the commission is paid to. Null when a partner is paid instead.

partner_id.description: The referral partner the commission is paid to, if any.

goal_id.description: The goal that earned the commission.

closed_by_user_id.description: The teammate who last worked the contact when the deal closed.

deal_value.description: Value of the deal the commission is based on, cents.

flagged_for_clawback.description: True when the sale behind the commission was later refunded.

source_event_type.description:
What earned the commission: `disposition` for a call disposition that achieved
a goal, `web_event` for a tracked website event, `revenue` for a subscription
renewal under a recurring commission agreement.

source_event_id.description:
Id of the disposition event, web event or revenue event that earned it. For
`disposition`, this is the `disposition_event_id` sent in
`disposition.completed`.

name.description: `commission.pending` only. Null if the goal could not be read.

approved_by.description: `commission.approved` only. User id of the approver.

rejected_by.description:
`commission.rejected` only. User id of the teammate who rejected it, or null when
it was rejected automatically because the sale was refunded.

reason.description:
`commission.rejected` only. The reason the teammate gave, if any. For an automatic
rejection, a description of the refund that caused it.

paid_by.description: `commission.paid` only. User id of the teammate who marked it paid.

GoalTriggeredData.description: `data` of `goal.triggered`. The ids are kept and their records attached: `team`, `contact` (null when `contact_id` is null), and on disposition goals `user` and `call`. Web goals carry `visitor_id`, `session_id`, `event_id`, `event_name` and `page_url`. Call and disposition goals carry `source_type`, `user_id`, `disposition_id`, `call_id` and `commission_id` instead.

goal_value.description: The value you gave the goal, in whole dollars, not cents. Can be negative.

tag_ids.description: Tags the goal adds to the contact.

list_ids.description: Lists the goal adds the contact to.

contact_id.description: Null when the website visitor isn't linked to a contact. Always set on call and disposition goals.

visitor_id.description: Web goals only. The tracked website visitor.

event_id.description: Web goals only. The tracked website event that achieved the goal, not the webhook's `event_id`.

source_type.description: Call and disposition goals only. What achieved the goal.

user_id.description: Call and disposition goals only. The teammate who set the disposition.

disposition_id.description: Call and disposition goals only. The disposition that achieved the goal, such as `sold`.

call_id.description: Call and disposition goals only. The call that was dispositioned.

commission_id.description:
Call and disposition goals only. The pending commission the goal created, which
is also announced by `commission.pending`. Null when the goal pays no commission.

DispositionCompletedData.description: `data` of `disposition.completed`: the call disposition as it was evaluated against your goals. The ids are kept and their records attached: `team`, `user`, `contact`, `call` and `list`.

disposition_event_id.description:
Id of this evaluation. A commission it created carries the same value as
`commission.source_event_id`.

user_id.description: The teammate who set the disposition.

disposition_id.description: The disposition, with the same values as on `contact.call.disposition`, such as `sold` or `dnc`.

list_id.description: The list the call was dialed from.

list_name.description: Always null for call dispositions; read `list.list_name`.

calls_to_contact.description: How many calls your team has made to the contact. Null if it could not be counted.

goal_ids.description: The goals this disposition achieved. Empty when none matched.

DispositionGoalTriggeredData.description: `data` of `disposition.goal.triggered`. `team`, `user` and `contact` are attached; the ids inside `disposition` are not expanded.

user_id.description: The teammate who set the disposition.

goal_value.description: The value you gave the goal, in whole dollars, not cents.

disposition.description: The disposition that achieved the goal and the call it was set on.

commission_id.description: The pending commission the goal created, if it pays one.

DispositionSaleClosedData.description: `data` of `disposition.sale.closed`. Money fields are integer cents. `team`, `user`, `contact` and `call` are attached.

user_id.description: The teammate who closed the sale.

deal_value.description: The commission's deal value, cents. Null when the goal pays no commission.

commission_id.description: Null when the goal pays no commission.

commission_amount.description: The commission amount, cents. Null when the goal pays no commission.

user_id.description: The teammate who set the disposition.

list_id.description: The list the call was dialed from.

DomainEmailBounceData.description: `data` of `domain.email.bounce` and `domain.email.bounce_hard`, one recipient per event. `team`, and when the ids are set `email` and `contact`, are attached.

message_id.description: The message id the email was sent with.

email_id.description: The Drop Cowboy email that bounced. Null when the message was not sent from Drop Cowboy.

contact_id.description: The contact the bounced email was sent to. Null when unknown.

bounce_sub_type.description: The receiving server's reason category, such as `General`, `NoEmail`, `Suppressed` or `MailboxFull`.

diagnostic_code.description: The receiving server's response, when it gave one.

timestamp.description: When the bounce was processed, epoch milliseconds.

DomainEmailComplaintData.description: `data` of `domain.email.complaint`, one recipient per event. `team`, and when the ids are set `email` and `contact`, are attached.

message_id.description: The message id the email was sent with.

email_id.description: The Drop Cowboy email that was reported. Null when the message was not sent from Drop Cowboy.

contact_id.description: The contact the email was sent to. Null when unknown.

recipient.description: The address that marked the email as spam.

feedback_type.description: The complaint type reported by the recipient's mailbox provider, such as `abuse`. Absent when the provider did not give one.

timestamp.description: When the complaint was processed, epoch milliseconds.

BadRequest.description:
Invalid request parameters. The code in `type` depends on the route, for example
`validation-error`, `bad-request`, `invalid-request`, `invalid-parameters` or
`missing-parameters`; branch on `status`.

example.title: Validation Error
example.detail: Request validation failed

example.title: Unauthorized
example.detail: Invalid API key or secret

example.title: Forbidden
example.detail: Insufficient permissions for this operation

example.title: Not Found
example.detail: The requested resource was not found

DetectionKeyServiceUnavailable.description: The Detection key store could not be reached. Nothing was changed; retry.

example.title: Service Unavailable
example.detail: Detection key service is unavailable, try again

example.title: Conflict
example.detail: A resource with this identifier already exists

PaymentRequired.description:
Nothing was done because of billing: either the plan allotment and prepaid
balance are both empty, or the subscription payment failed and the account is
past due. Always problem details with `type` `.../errors/payment-required`.
When the account is past due, email and campaign routes add
`details.dunning_tier` (`restricted`, `suspended` or `canceled`). Top up or fix
the payment method in the dashboard, then retry.

value.title: Payment Required
value.detail: Your subscription payment didn't go through, so sending is paused. This is separate from your messaging funds balance. Update your payment method to resume sending campaigns.

TooManyRequests.description:
Your account went over the rate limit of 1,500 requests per second, with bursts
to 2,000, across all routes. Retry with exponential backoff and jitter.

ServerError.description: Unexpected failure. Safe to retry idempotent reads; for writes, check state first.

example.title: Server Error
example.detail: Internal error

InsufficientScope.description: The credentials are valid but lack every scope this operation accepts.

example.title: Insufficient Scope
example.detail: This endpoint requires one of: contacts:read

SendBadRequest.description:
Nothing was sent. The body was empty, was not a JSON object or was larger than
256 KB, or `x-key`, `x-secret`, `Authorization` or `Idempotency-Key` contained
characters other than printable ASCII. Fix the request before retrying.

value.title: Validation Error
value.detail: The request body must be a non-empty JSON object.

notQueued.summary: Body too large or headers not printable ASCII

value.title: Validation Error
value.detail: The request could not be queued. The body must be JSON under 256 KB and the X-Key, X-Secret, Authorization and Idempotency-Key headers must be printable ASCII.

SendMissingCredentials.description:
The request carried no credentials: neither a non-blank `x-key` and `x-secret`
pair nor an `Authorization: Bearer` token. Nothing was sent. Credentials that
are present but wrong (a bad key or secret, or a token that is invalid, expired
or lacks the send scope) are not caught here: they get `202`, and the failure
(`reason_code` 3007, Not authorized) is posted to `callback_url` only.

example.title: Unauthorized
example.detail: Send an API key in X-Key and X-Secret, or an access token in Authorization: Bearer.

SendNotQueued.description:
We couldn't queue the request and nothing was sent. Retry with backoff and the
same `Idempotency-Key`. This body is not a problem-details object.

SendQueueNoReceipt.description:
We couldn't confirm the request was queued. Retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key`: if the first attempt went through, the retry is skipped as a
duplicate.

example.title: Bad Gateway
example.detail: The message was not queued. It is safe to retry.

KnowledgeForbidden.description:
Either the credentials lack the scope (`insufficient-scope`), or the caller is a
signed-in user whose role cannot use or manage AI agents (`forbidden`, with
`detail` "You do not have permission to use Knowledge Bases." on reads or
"You do not have permission to manage Knowledge Bases." on changes). Team API
keys are never limited by role. If the role cannot be looked up the answer is
`500` (`server-error`) instead.

value.title: Insufficient Scope
value.detail: This endpoint requires one of: agents:write

role.summary: User role cannot manage knowledge bases

value.title: Forbidden
value.detail: You do not have permission to manage Knowledge Bases.

AgentForbidden.description:
Either the credentials lack the scope (`insufficient-scope`), or the caller is a
signed-in user whose role does not allow it (`forbidden`). `detail` is
"You do not have permission to manage AI Agents." when the role has no AI agent
access, or "Not authorized to perform this AI chat action" when the role may not
create, change, delete or publish agents. Team API keys are never limited by
role. If the role cannot be looked up the answer is `500` (`server-error`)
instead.
